description.p: Lectern opens a Markdown file and shows it, the way a document viewer shows a PDF. There is no editing interface and no sidebar: open a file, read it, search it, print it.
Documents are rendered with native GTK widgets rather than an embedded browser engine, so the app starts instantly and the text behaves like text everywhere else in the desktop.

ul.li: CommonMark and GitHub-Flavored Markdown: tables, task lists, footnotes and strikethrough
Fenced code blocks with syntax highlighting
Find, with whole-word and case-sensitive options, that searches table cells too
Automatic reload when the file changes on disk, keeping your place

description.p: Images hosted on the web are not fetched when a document is opened. Opening a file should not tell whoever hosts its images that you opened it, so remote images load only when you ask for them.

screenshot.caption: A document with a table, task list and highlighted code
Fenced code blocks are syntax highlighted
Find matches text inside table cells as well as body text

description.p: Lectern now keeps a list of recently opened documents. It appears on the start screen, below the Open button, and in an "Open Recent" submenu in the main menu, most recently opened first. Choosing a file from the start screen opens it in the current window instead of leaving an empty one behind, and Ctrl+O opens the file chooser from anywhere.
The list is the desktop's own recent-files store, shared with the file manager and other applications.

Printing now always uses a light color scheme, regardless of the desktop's dark mode, so code blocks and diagrams no longer come out with dark backgrounds on a white page. Page margins are wider and asymmetric, and the header/footer option — now on by default — leaves proper clearance around the page number and running head instead of sitting flush against the text.
"Print to File" now suggests the document's own file name instead of a generic "output.pdf", and the header/footer preference is remembered per document across restarts.
Fedora packages are now available via COPR.

Printing gains proper page margins and an optional header and footer, toggled from the hamburger menu. Pagination now keeps a heading with the section it introduces and avoids stranding a single line at the top or bottom of a page.

Copying a selection now puts rich HTML and Markdown on the clipboard alongside plain text, so pasting into an editor like Thunderbird or a word processor keeps formatting, tables, images and diagrams intact rather than flattening everything to plain text.
Lectern is now translatable, and ships with translations for Danish, Spanish, German, French, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, Chinese (Simplified), Korean, Finnish, Swedish and Norwegian Bokmål.
The About dialog shows the app's own icon instead of a generic placeholder.

Mermaid diagrams in fenced code blocks are now drawn, rather than shown as source. Flowcharts, sequence diagrams, class diagrams and entity-relationship diagrams are painted natively, so they appear in printouts too and no browser engine is involved. Anything outside the supported subset still falls back to a highlighted code block.
Body text no longer runs the full width of the window: it is capped at a comfortable measure and centred, the way a page of prose should read on a wide screen.

Zooming now scales the whole layout. Line spacing, block gaps, indents and margins grow and shrink with the text instead of staying put, so a document reads the same at every zoom level. Line height, list spacing and the space around nested lists have been brought in line with how the same Markdown renders on GitHub.
Corrects the project URLs after the repository was renamed, so the screenshots and links point at their permanent locations rather than relying on a redirect.
